slides.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE A FUSS A display of unnecessary or excessive excitement, activity, or interest I don't know what all the fuss is about. A SCAM A deceptive scheme or trick used to cheat someone out of something, especially money The buying of the cars turned out to be just a scam. A STORM IN A TEACUP A small event that has been exaggerated out of proportion It was not that serious. Stop making a storm in a teacup. A CHARADE An absurd pretense intended to create a pleasant or respectable appearance I will ask Tina to cut the charade off. A LIP SERVICE An expression of agreement that is not supported by real conviction We cannot believe for a second the lip service given by the candidate. A SNOW JOB A deception or a fraud It is all a snow job, isn’t it? A SHARP PRACTICE A deceitful sneaky practice After the sharp practice was discovered the government has been keeping a closer eye on the private sector. A FISH TALE A lie or an exaggeration of the truth I don’t think he was telling the truth, it sounded like nothing but a good old fish tale to me.

slides.title: Structures QUESTIONS TAG QUESTIONS Simple Present Are you in the school? Do you have a dog? You are in school, aren’t you? You have a dog, don’t you? Present Progressive Is he calling his mother?. He is not calling his mother, is he?. Past simple Was she at Jake’s last night?. She was at Jake’s last night, wasn’t she? Past Progressive Were you just talking to Mat? You were just talking to Mat, weren’t you? Future Will he buy the car? Are you going to cook dinner? He will buy the car, won’t he? You are not going to cook dinner, are you? Present Perfect Has he flown to China already? He has already flown to China, hasn’t he?

Any tense can be used to look for confirmation. Check the chart and learn about tag questions.

slides.title: Structures QUESTIONS TAG QUESTIONS Past Perfect Had Mike taken English lessons by 2020? He had taken English lessons by 2020, hadn't he? Modals Can you go come with me? Would they join us? Should she call first? Must they have a review? You can’t come with me, can you?. They would join us, wouldn’t they?. She should call first, shouldn’t she?. They must have a review, musn’t they? To Consider 1. Tag questions are used at the end of the sentences. 2. Tag questions are used to with any tense as you see in the examples. 3. If the statement is positive, the tag question goes negative. 4. If the statement is negative, the tag question goes positive. 5. If the subject is ‘I’, the tag questions works with aren’t. E.G. I am right, aren’t I? 6. Using the expression Let’s makes us work with the word shall. E.G. Let’s go, shall we? 7. When having Imperatives, we work with will. E.G. Close the door, will you? 8. Affirmative tags after affirmative statements can be used to express interest or surprise. E.G. You are leaving home, are you?

slides.title: We can use tag questions for the following functions:
visibleTexts: We can use tag questions for the following functions:

Functions Examples 1 Check or confirm information You can’t swim, can you? They are not coming, are they? 2 Ask for agreement The food was delicious, wasn’t it? You love this movie, don’t you? 3 Wish to know the truth They were married, weren’t they? You have not told them, have you? 4. Express surprise or Interest You made this draft, did you? You had planned it all, had you?

To consider 1. If you pronounce the tag question with a rising intonation, the utterance will declare uncertainty. 2. If you pronounce the tag question with falling intonation, the utterance will declare certainty; you just need confirmation.

C. Read the following paragraph and extract sentences with tag questions. What function are they representing. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher.

You know what it means, don’t you? It would be definitely amazing if we spoke at least three or four languages naturally, wouldn’t it? However, the reality is that most people are exposed to two languages or three as a top when being kids, which means that acquiring others would take time and dedication during life. Additionally, we all need to understand that learning a language requires a big effort, and that it will not come out of the blue will it? For instance, attending classes and looking for professional help are the first steps we have to take into account, but there is also the need for giving ourselves the chance to practice outside classes, opening spaces where we are in touch with the language and of course use what we learn. However, there are many who think that just attending lessons is enough, don’t they? Also, that there is no need to listen or to check what there was in my previous lesson in order to acquire a good level. Sadly, thinking like that only leads to self - frustration since those people learn the hard way that learning a language means so much more than coming to class, doesn’t it?
